classification.difficultyReason: Students read the signed multiplier and vertical shift from the rule and choose to apply the reflection and stretch before translating so the shift remains 2.

content.prompt: Bob is asked to sketch $y=2-3\sqrt{x}$ using a vertical translation, vertical dilation, and a reflection, in an order of his choosing. Although it is possible to do it in more than one way, which order will be easier for Bob?

answer.short: Reflect across the $x$-axis, dilate vertically by a factor of $3$, then translate up $2$ units.
answer.worked: Reflect $y=\sqrt{x}$ to get $y=-\sqrt{x}$, then triple the heights to get $y=-3\sqrt{x}$. Translate up $2$ units to get $y=2-3\sqrt{x}$. The reflection and dilation can also be swapped because both multiply the output. Translating last lets Bob use the shift of $2$ directly.
